findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Various types of milks were observed not date marked throughout the facility. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that TCF food items stored in house longer than 24 hours are date marked and discarded if not used within 7 days of opening. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed a box of single service cups sitting on the floor under the counter in the kitchen. Store all single service items at least 6" off the floor at all times.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed a scoop inside the bulk flour container to have the handle in contact with the flour. Store handles so as not to be in contact with foods to prevent contamination.
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the dish machine to have limescale build up and a drawer pull on the prep table to be missing a screw on one side. Kitchen staff states dish machine is serviced on a monthly basis and service is due any time. Ds-scale the dish machine and repair drawer pull.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Did not observe a date mark on the opened bag of shredded cheese.  The cheese was opened last week  per Ms. Baker.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. 
*Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.comment:
Did not observe a test kit for checking sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1200 The floor drain beneath the three-part sink is missing a cover. Provide a proper cover over the floor drain prevent food from falling into the plumbing. There is a proper grate over the dishmachine floor drain. ALSO, the floor by the backdoor hasa tile that is beginning to peel back. This allows for food debris and water to accumulate. Properly secure the floor so the surface is smooth, easily cleanable and non-absorbent. All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings. 750-1220 The handsink is not properly caulked to the wall and the drywall is becoming soft and wet from handwashing splash. Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.
